principles.principle: Mandate: review and propose; deference to Commission except where effective representation is better served

quotes.text: The advisory panel did not sit in appeal of the 2025-2026 Electoral Boundaries Commissions recommendations. Nor was the panel bound by the Commission's proposals.

deference was given to the proposals of the 2025-2026 Electoral Boundaries Commission, except where some or all of the advisory panel's members were of the view that a different area or boundary of an electoral division might better achieve effective representation based on recognized and statutorily prescribed considerations.
the advisory panel deferred to most, but not all, of the Commission's electoral boundary recommendations.
We saw our task as one of identifying alterations which might better achieve effective representation.

principles.principle: 'Necessary' modifications and the Chairman's 'maintain the rest of the province' condition

quotes.text: The Chairman's direction that "The rest of the province as we propose must be maintained to the extent possible" would, if followed, render inoperative the Legislature's direction to the panel that it review all the Province`s electoral boundaries and make proposals with respect to their area, boundaries and names.
the Government Motion's earlier direction to review and make proposals with respect to the Province's electoral divisions made it "necessary" to adjust that so-called condition.

subject to any modifications the independent advisory panel considers necessary, taking into consideration the requirement for effective representation as guaranteed by the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
Reasonable people can reasonably disagree. There are no right answers. There are wrong answers, admittedly, but no right ones.

principles.principle: Restoring the two rural divisions cascades into neighbouring divisions

quotes.text: Changes to the boundaries of one electoral division or the insertion of a "new" electoral division in already mapped territory requires changes to the boundaries of electoral divisions elsewhere.
Adding two electoral divisions is like adding two pieces to an already-completed jig saw puzzle. Adjustments had to be made.
Because of that restoration, the panel has also been able to recommend arguably more logical electoral divisions along Highway 2 between Calgary and Edmonton.
The restoration of the Rocky Mountain House-Sundre electoral division gave the advisory panel the opportunity to reconfigure the Highway 2 corridor electoral divisions.

principles.principle: Preserve the status quo absent a pressing need

quotes.text: in the absence of a pressing need to make changes, maintaining the status quo is considered good practice in electoral boundary mapping.
Preserving the status quo is a good thing in electoral boundary mapping, absent contrary considerations of which there are none.
It preserves the status quo and avoids the incongruous encirclement of the City of Lethbridge that the Commission's recommendation entailed.
the advisory panel is recommending that the current (2017) electoral division be roughly maintained in its prior configuration.

principles.principle: Communities of interest, not municipal boundaries, shape divisions

quotes.text: Communities of interest are shaped by transportation corridors, employment, shared services, shared recreation facilities, golf courses, bike routes, soccer pitches, shared schools, etc. Municipal boundaries in and of themselves have little to do with communities of interest in circumstances like those existing in west Calgary and Springbank.
The first is communities of interest: Southern Alberta is uniquely united economically around the agricultural and food processing industries which transcend the boundaries of the City of Lethbridge.
The panel is recommending electoral boundaries that reflect those lived relationships rather than treat the city limits as an impermeable wall.

Support for the assertion that South Springbank is very much a Calgary community can be found in the fact that there are two 18-hole golf courses, one 27-hole golf course and one 45-hole golf course located in South Springbank.
Communities of interest may supersede these factors.

principles.principle: Urban-with-urban is not a true hybrid; true hybrids mix urban and rural (agrarian) interests

quotes.text: True hybrids mix people with fundamentally different interests. Hybrid ridings mix urban and rural (agrarian) residents in electoral divisions.
It mixes urban with urban residents. It does not mix much rural with urban.
It is simply an electoral division which straddles a municipal boundary, uniting for electoral purposes only, suburban residents of the City with suburban residents of Rockyview County.
The hybrids proposed by the advisory panel for Calgary were not hybrids at all according to the foregoing definition.
Where the concern arises is when the hybrid mixes populations of demonstrably different interests.

principles.principle: Hybrids are legitimate and widespread; test is genuine community of interest or population need

quotes.text: The Commission concluded, as many boundaries commissions before it concluded, that one cannot draw an electoral map of Alberta which achieves effective representation without creating hybrid electoral divisions.

The relevant question is therefore not whether hybrids are permissible or desirable, but whether a proposed hybrid reflects a genuine community of interest or is needed to achieve population-compliance.
the need to ensure effective representation for all Albertans may necessitate at times that a hybrid be used purely to satisfy the numerical challenge across the province that a Commission faces.
The factors noted above are to be used as guidelines rather than definite characteristics for each hybrid constituency.

Hybridization works both ways. It can help cities receive the representation they need. It can help rural electoral divisions to obtain the population they need to be relatively compact and manageable.

principles.principle: Lethbridge 'population to spare' / borrowing population from a city for rural divisions

quotes.text: Lethbridge already has population to spare.

if it grows any more, its population will have to be shared with electoral divisions outside of Lethbridge because it will have too much population for two electoral divisions and not enough population for three electoral divisions.
Borrowing population to create electoral divisions of a manageable size is legitimate electoral mapping.

What is different is that Lethbridge is being asked to share some of its population with adjoining electoral divisions in order to ensure that they can remain primarily southern Alberta constituencies.
borrowing population from the perimeters of the City of Lethbridge to achieve relative population parity and to reflect shared community interests.
The other is to "borrow population" from nearby urban municipalities which share the same communities of interest as their rural (agrarian) neighbours.

principles.principle: Rural area next to a town lends population; converse of Lethbridge (adjacent area assists a mid-size city)

quotes.text: Here is an example of where an area adjacent to an urban municipality assists it in getting more effective representation. In the south of the Province, the advisory panel recommends the converse, namely that an urban municipality (Lethbridge) share some of its population in order that adjacent rural populations obtain more effective representation.

principles.principle: Regional representation in southern Alberta

quotes.text: the reason the panel recommends these changes is to achieve better regional representation of the people of southern Alberta.
This is not hybridization for an improper purpose. It is a model grounded in the desire to achieve effective representation.
Around Lethbridge, the answer to both questions is yes.
Perhaps nowhere else in Alberta is there a clearer shared community of interests than in Southern Alberta around Lethbridge.

principles.principle: Mid-size towns and cities get their own representative

the current boundaries of Lesser Slave Lake make it eligible for Section 15(2) status without additional territory being added.

principles.principle: Highway corridors unite divisions

the advisory panel was able to recommend an electoral division that put Lacombe back into an electoral division focused on the Highway 2 Corridor rather than on the West Country.

principles.principle: Keep municipalities / counties / reserves whole or together

quotes.text: to keep most of Sturgeon County united in a single electoral division.

minimal population variance tells you little about the merit of any particular electoral division or electoral map.

principles.principle: Restraint where input is thin: where to stop (Church Ranches)

principles.principle: Partisan effect is not gerrymandering; purpose is

quotes.text: It is not a gerrymander to recommend or approve an electoral boundary change that favours or disadvantages a party or a candidate. All changes to electoral boundaries have the potential to do that.

so long as that second look is done with a view to achieving a more effective representation, not with a view to giving an electoral advantage to any political party or to any incumbent

keep stable communities together, manage edge growth deliberately and use rural or exurban additions only when they serve a coherent boundary purpose.

Calgary-East is the logical growth-management division because it lies on the city's edge and can absorb developing communities without fragmenting stable inner neighbourhoods.

Together, these neighbourhoods form a coherent electoral community. Keeping them together supports community-of-interest principles and avoids dividing a recognizable part of northeast Calgary without a clear boundary rationale.
For northeast Calgary, this process would have identified early that drawing every new division near the average left too little capacity for known growth.

minority_counter.text: The newly proposed boundaries for these four electoral divisions are also less rectangular and less clear than those in the ABEBC Majority Report, even if they are much more logical than the ABEBC Minority Report.
Our colleagues do not justify such a material departure from boundaries that create a more equal distribution of population as set out in the ABEBC Majority Report

divisions.note: Executive summary says no improvements were recommended; the minority treats the discussion as a proposal to 'consider' changes. Population table at p062: Cross 61,800 (+15%), Klein 62,300 (+16%), East 58,300 (+9%), Confluence 51,000 (-5%).

divisions.change: Calgary-North West extended west to include Bearspaw subdivisions south of Highway 1A (Bearspaw Village, Watermark, etc.); Church Ranches and others north of Highway 1A left for future consideration.

reasons.text: The 2025-2026 Electoral Boundaries Commission gave "serious consideration" to moving "Bearspaw" into the Calgary-North West electoral division

the electoral division recommended by not only the 2025-2026 Electoral Boundaries Commission, but also by the 2017 Electoral Boundaries Commission and the 2010 Electoral Boundaries Commission did in fact cross 12-Mile Coulee Road at the south end to take in the two Bearspaw communities
Clearly the ties to Calgary are greater.
Two busy golf courses, riding arenas, Haskayne Legacy Park and the Glenbow Ranch Provincial Park are places where thousands of Calgary residents recreate on a regular basis
But there is definitely a case to be made for also including Church Ranches.

minority_counter.text: Including Bearspaw Village in Calgary-North West is the most defensible change proposed by our colleagues.
Bearspaw Village, though urban to some extent, is a distinct residential community with acreage infrastructure and independent utility systems.
Accordingly, it is our view that reasonable people can disagree about where these communities belong.

divisions.note: Minority calls this the most defensible of the majority's changes but not 'necessary'.

divisions.change: Calgary-Bow extended west to take in North Springbank (north of the TransCanada, south of the Bow River, east of Highway 22); about 58,673 or 9% above average.

reasons.text: The advisory panel proposes that Springbank be paired with either Calgary-Bow or Calgary-West depending on what side of the TransCanada Highway its residents live.

But, in its Final Report, the majority members stated that they chose not to include Springbank in this electoral division because it would make the population too large. The advisory panel respectfully disagrees.

Including Springbank in the electoral division results in a population of roughly 9% above the average electoral division's population for all 91 of the Province's electoral divisions. That is well within the permitted variances.

It is simply an electoral division which straddles or extends beyond the city limits into a high growth area where urban-like development has long since taken place. It mixes urban with urban residents.
the TransCanada Highway is a fairly substantial natural boundary.
The criticism that the advisory panel's proposal would extend the Calgary-Bow electoral riding 30 km from Calgary's western border is disingenuous.

minority_counter.text: However, we also have no doubt that many residents of Bearspaw and Springbank have consciously chosen not to live in Calgary, and desire that to be reflected in their representation.
Even if we were to accept that effective representation requires Springbank to be in a Calgary electoral division, we find dividing it between Calgary-West and Calgary-Bow to be odd.
However, the West Calgary maps subtly dilute Calgarians' votes in ways that are not necessary to achieve effective representation.
The addition of two new electoral divisions means that the legislature has entirely solved the problem through "a)". Use of "c)" is accordingly unnecessary.

divisions.note: Majority states this was not unanimous: 'We were not all agreed, but the majority proposes' (p069).

divisions.change: Calgary West-Elbow Valley replaced by Calgary-West-Springbank: all South Springbank (south of TransCanada, north of Elbow River) joins Calgary West.

reasons.text: We concur in what the 2025-2026 Electoral Boundaries Commission in extending Calgary-West into Rocky View County along Highway 8 and its reasons therefor.

The electoral division we propose would have a much more regular polygon shape with straight line boundaries, as opposed to the long, narrow, meandering salamander shape of Calgary-West-Elbow Valley recommended by the Commission.
The splitting of Springbank along the Elbow River was worse.
And because there are almost no commercial services in South Springbank, residents there must commute into Calgary for their daily needs.

In conclusion, the advisory panel proposes that the Legislature consider approving the Calgary-West-Springbank electoral division as the panel has proposed it, rather than put South Springbank in a Cochrane electoral division.

minority_counter.text: Unlike Elbow Valley, which is integrated into Calgary's wastewater system (warranting the differential treatment between Elbow Valley and Bearspaw and Springbank), these communities receive few if any municipal services from Calgary.
Dividing Springbank was never proposed to the ABEBC.
This is another reason we are skeptical of the inclusion of Bearspaw and Springbank in Calgary electoral divisions.

divisions.note: Minority table 1 (p142) treats Calgary West-Elbow Valley (30 km) as an accepted add-on hybrid.

divisions.change: Cochrane no longer paired with Springbank; stands as its own division with about 48,000 people (11% below average) and its own representative.

reasons.text: What the 2025-2026 Electoral Boundaries Commission did made sense, but the advisory panel believes that Springbank's connection to Calgary is even stronger than its connection to Cochrane.
However the way the advisory panel has mapped the Cochrane electoral division, it still has about 48,000 people in it or about 11% below average.

removing Springbank north of the TransCanada Highway from the Cochrane electoral division reduces the population of the Cochrane electoral division from roughly 6% below average to almost 13% below average.
Those farmers and ranchers might be more connected to Cochrane than Calgary, but they are a shrinking minority.

minority_counter.text: Our colleagues have recommended breaking up the proposed Cochrane-Springbank electoral division because they disagree with the ABEBC Majority's rationale that it was necessary to maintain an appropriate population balance for the electoral divisions. Yet the links between Diamond Valley and Banff and Canmore are far weaker than the links between Springbank and Cochrane.

divisions.note: Majority's own figures differ: 'about 48,000 ... 11% below' (p077) vs 'almost 13% below average' (p070).

divisions.change: One Lethbridge-only division of about 60,000 (about 60% of the city's population): downtown, most of West Lethbridge, and east/southeast communities.

reasons.text: The advisory panel proposes one Lethbridge electoral division that is made up solely of Lethbridge and three other hybrid electoral divisions made up of Lethbridge residents and residents of towns, villages, and rural areas of Southern Alberta.

It is a distinct urban electoral division with higher density and rental housing, downtown commerce, civic and cultural institutions, social health services, transit dependencies and established (older) neighborhood concerns.
Lethbridge has grown large and diverse enough to contain a distinct inner-city community of interest that warrants separate representation and its own electoral division.

minority_counter.text: Essentially, our colleagues have taken one of Lethbridge's two urban seats away and replaced it with a rural electoral division of Lethbridge-Little Bow.
Lethbridge is a city of approximately 110,000 people. Its residents and leaders clearly want two MLAs
Finally, we must respectfully observe that this map of the Lethbridge area bears all the hallmarks of a practice called "packing".
We also view the agricultural link in this area to be of minimal importance in drawing electoral boundaries.

divisions.note: Majority states the southern Alberta proposals are supported by 'three of the five advisory panel members' (p082).

divisions.change: Re-establishes Little Bow with a contiguous part of NE Lethbridge and a bit of West Lethbridge, along Highways 23/24 north to the Siksika reserve.

reasons.text: Re-establishing a Little Bow electoral division would restore a historically coherent voice for communities tied by Highways 23 and 24, irrigation, intensive agriculture and the Lethbridge-area agricultural services

The proposed electoral division therefore would provide population balance and "connects" the rural electoral division to the urban services, employment and processing capacity in Lethbridge upon which much of the Little Bow population depends.
The same rural Southern Alberta population deficiency that has existed for years persists to this day.
in order to prevent Little Bow, a new electoral division recommended by the panel, from becoming too large.

minority_counter.text: there are 80 km between the border of Lethbridge and the southern border of Lethbridge-Cardston, 120 km to the northern border of Lethbridge-Little Bow, and 150 km to the southeastern border of Lethbridge-Taber-Warner.

We also note that our colleagues' proposed electoral division of Lethbridge-Little Bow extends north of the Siksika Reserve such that residents would be travelling to Calgary rather than Lethbridge for government services.

divisions.change: Re-establishes Lethbridge-Taber-Warner with 6,679 people from east/southeast Lethbridge, organized around Highways 3 and 4.

reasons.text: Including a small population from Lethbridge (6,679 people) in the electoral division provides a practical way to give this electoral division a population which meets statutory requirements and yet remains geographically manageable.
The electoral division possesses a more understandable community of shared interests than a geographically huge corridor assembled from far-flung municipalities with limited daily interaction.
What the minority members of the 2025-2026 Electoral Boundaries Commission recommended was not substantively unreasonable.

minority_counter.text: However, this does not mean that the people of Lethbridge intrinsically see these people as part of their community nor does it mean that the people visiting Lethbridge see themselves as part of that community.
Unlike Medicine Hat, the population math is near-perfect for Lethbridge to get its desire.

divisions.change: Re-establishes a Cardston division (Cardston, Raymond, Magrath, Blood Reserve) borrowing about 17,000 people from Lethbridge.

reasons.text: Another solution to this population disparity problem is the creation of a Cardston, Magrath, Raymond, and Blood Reserve electoral division that borrows population from the City of Lethbridge (roughly 17,000 people).
The advisory panel's recommendation might better withstand the test of time and future population increases than the perfectly understandable recommendation of the Commission.
As evidence of that, at one point, the panel even considered making Cardston a special electoral division under Section 15(2) of the Act.

minority_counter.text: Hybridizing Lethbridge to such a significant extent does not fit into any of the three examples of hybrid electoral divisions that we cite above.

Our colleagues further suggest that this redraw is necessary because more significant hybridization will need to occur in Lethbridge at the next redistribution and it is prudent to draw electoral divisions that will be durable.
There is no need to thrust a highly disruptive, unnecessary map onto Lethbridge when the present numbers do not require it

divisions.change: Livingstone-Macleod reconfigured north-south along Highways 3 and 2 (Fort Macleod, Pincher Creek, Crowsnest to High River); Coaldale, Picture Butte and Turin removed.

reasons.text: The configuration the advisory panel proposes is admittedly driven by its Lethbridge and Little Bow recommendations north of Lethbridge and by its Taber-Warner recommendations east of Lethbridge.
It preserves the status quo and avoids the incongruous encirclement of the City of Lethbridge that the Commission's recommendation entailed.
It is not the most desirable electoral division in the Province because of its size and shape.

minority_counter.text: removing the population of these municipalities from their rural neighbouring electoral divisions creates cascading effects that are clearly unreasonable

divisions.note: The minority does not discuss Macleod-Crowsnest by name; the counter-quote is its general cascade objection about Coaldale/Coalhurst.

divisions.change: Canmore-Banff/Banff-Kananaskis gains Longview, Diamond Valley, Millarville, Priddis, Bragg Creek and Bearspaw reserve (Highway 22 corridor) so it does not need s.15(2); loses northeast territory to Rocky Mountain House-Sundre and Springbank.

reasons.text: So the advisory panel is recommending against conferring Section 15(2) status on these two high-end vacation home communities or any electoral division which contains them.

But the Act does mandate that the population of ordinary electoral divisions must not be more than 25% below the average population. The addition of Diamond Valley and nearby hamlets or villages adds population of this electoral division.
the connection of Diamond Valley, Millarville, Priddis and Bragg Creek to Kananaskis and Banff is arguably stronger than that the connection of Springbank to Banff.
Banff, Canmore, Kananaskis, Longview, Diamond Valley, Millarville, Priddis and Bragg Creek form a logically connected mountain-foothills community of interest.
Finally, separating Diamond Valley from Okotoks gives Okotoks its own representative to which it will soon be entitled if it continues to grow the way it has.

minority_counter.text: By comparison, Diamond Valley's Chamber of Commerce listing has two hotels.
Not a single submission, to our knowledge, asked for Diamond Valley to be paired with Banff.
Separating them to add population to the Canmore-Banff electoral division makes little sense.
We cannot build electoral boundaries today on what may or may not develop economically in the next 10-20 years.
Revisiting this determination is another collateral attack on the ABEBC Majority Report holdings

divisions.change: Okotoks separated from Diamond Valley (which moves to Banff-Canmore-Diamond Valley); the majority covers this only inside the Banff-Canmore-Diamond Valley section and in the Cochrane/Springbank section.

reasons.text: Finally, separating Diamond Valley from Okotoks gives Okotoks its own representative to which it will soon be entitled if it continues to grow the way it has.
similar-sized cities such as Okotoks, Airdrie and Spruce Grove will have dedicated representation in the Legislature if the advisory panel's proposals are approved.

minority_counter.text: Moreover, there was overwhelming desire for Okotoks and Diamond Valley to be paired in the same electoral division after the ABEBC Interim Report.

divisions.note: No separate Okotoks narrative in the majority text; its map page carries no prose.

divisions.change: No majority reason found. The minority names Red Deer-South as a boundary it disagrees with (with Blackfalds-Innisfail), the Red Deer portion.

reasons.text: The panel also proposes to borrow a bit of population from Red Deer to give the Blackfalds-Innisfail the population it needs.

minority_counter.text: We also disagree, although not as strongly, with our colleagues' proposed boundaries of Red Deer-South and Blackfalds-Innisfail.

divisions.note: The majority never discusses Red Deer-South by name in prose; only the Red Deer borrowing for Blackfalds-Innisfail (p055, p113).
